findings.title: Cleanup in the new test removes a non-existent IdP "alias" instead of the created IdP
findings.body: The cleanup registration `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets the literal alias "alias", not the `idp-alias-<i>` provider just created. The 20 IdPs created by testCacheIDPForLogin are therefore never removed. They persist into later tests in the class and into other tests sharing the realm, which can change realm-wide IdP counts and login-list results. The same copy-paste bug appears at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`. Use the actual alias, e.g. `final String alias = ...; getCleanup().addCleanup(() -> testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias).remove());`.

findings.title: remove() now always performs an extra DB lookup of the IdP by alias
findings.body: `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is executed unconditionally at the top of remove(). Previously the DB lookup only happened in the branch where the alias cache entry was invalidated. Now every removal pays an additional query even when the cache-based branch is taken, and the result is used only to compute login-cache invalidation. This is a small but avoidable cost on a write path.

findings.title: getForLogin Javadoc does not describe the new organization public-broker requirement
findings.body: The Javadoc says an IdP can be used for login if it is enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. The predicate change in LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() now also requires that an IdP linked to an organization has BROKER_PUBLIC=true. That condition is missing from the documented contract, so implementers and callers of getLoginPredicate()/getForLogin cannot tell from the interface what qualifies an org-linked IdP for login.
